target_learners: university undergraduate students in an academic writing course (1-2 sections, ~30-60 students, including ESL learners)
learning_goals: independently plan, draft and revise academic writing without AI
use AI writing assistants critically as formative feedback and error-explanation tools, not as text generators
develop reflection skills: explain every AI-assisted change in their own words

phase_1.name: Phase 1 — Independent Drafting (No AI)
activities: weeks 1-2: students draft essays with no AI access whatsoever
phase_1.ai_usage_rule: all AI usage forbidden; drafts must be entirely student-written
phase_1.outcome_check: baseline independent writing quality and no-AI baseline score

phase_2.name: Phase 2 — AI Feedback and Error Explanation Only
activities: weeks 3-4: AI allowed to give feedback on student drafts and explain grammar/style errors; it must not generate new text
phase_2.ai_usage_rule: AI may give formative feedback and explain errors only; no generation or rewriting of passages
phase_2.outcome_check: mid-pilot in-class writing sample without AI; student reflection on which feedback was applied

phase_3.name: Phase 3 — AI-Assisted Revision with Explanation
activities: weeks 5-7: AI may suggest revisions; students must accept/reject each suggestion and justify their choices in a revision memo
phase_3.ai_usage_rule: AI-assisted revision allowed only with a mandatory revision memo explaining every AI-suggested change that was kept
phase_3.outcome_check: weekly draft quality rubric plus revision-memo completeness

phase_4.name: Phase 4 — Independent Writing Transfer Test (No AI)
activities: week 8: a new academic writing task on an unseen topic completed in a strictly no-AI environment
phase_4.ai_usage_rule: no AI access during the transfer assessment
phase_4.outcome_check: independent writing score and transfer-task rubric

ai_usage_policy: AI usage is restricted to three explicitly graded modes: no-AI drafting (phase 1), feedback/error-explanation only (phase 2), AI-assisted revision with mandatory explanation (phase 3). Copying AI-generated text into a submission without explanation is an academic integrity violation. A no-AI transfer assessment closes the pilot (phase 4).
teacher_role: design guardrailed feedback prompts and rubrics; review AI usage logs and revision memos weekly; hold short reflection debriefs
student_role: draft independently in phase 1; use AI only for feedback in phase 2; revise with AI while documenting every change in phase 3; complete the independent no-AI transfer task in phase 4
reflection_requirement: students must explain every AI-assisted change in their own words (revision memo); one written reflection per phase on when AI helped versus when it masked understanding
assessment: no-AI baseline writing assessment, mid-pilot in-class writing sample, draft quality rubric, independent no-AI writing transfer task, revision memos, AI usage self-report
risk_control: guardrailed usage policy modeled on Bastani 2026 GPT Tutor (feedback/hints instead of answers)
independent no-AI writing transfer test prevents score inflation from AI-supported task performance
revision memos and usage logs reviewed weekly to detect AI dependency
academic integrity policy explicitly covers AI-generated text and unexamined copying
false-confidence check: predicted grade vs actual grade on no-AI assessments
stop_conditions: independent writing transfer-test scores drop significantly below baseline/cohort expectations
revision memos show widespread unexamined AI copying (integrity violations in >20% of submissions)
AI dependency signals (usage without understanding, explanation quality) exceed threshold for two consecutive weeks
teacher workload for reviewing memos/logs becomes unsustainable
